_comment: Deliberately JSON, not YAML: this file is loaded unchanged by the Dart on-device port. Adding a YAML parser to the phone build is avoidable weight. Every rule carries an id so that each intervention is auditable and reportable.
disclaimer: This is general medication information, not medical advice. Always confirm with a pharmacist, nurse or doctor before acting on it.

input_rules.description: Any indication of intent to use medication to self-harm. Highest priority: checked before every other rule.
Requests for dangerous, toxic or fatal quantities of any substance.
Requests for a specific dose or dosing schedule. The model must never supply one.
Dosing in children. Weight-based and never safe to generalise.
Medication use in pregnancy or while breastfeeding.
Stopping, substituting or altering a prescribed regimen.
Recreational use, or obtaining prescription medicine without a prescription.

output_rules.description: Model produced a number adjacent to a dose unit. Suppress the whole response.
Model asserted a diagnosis. Out of scope for a medication-information assistant.
output_rules.regex: \byou (?:have|are suffering from|have got|likely have|probably have)\b|\bthis (?:means|indicates) (?:you|that you) (?:have|are)\b|\byou(?:'re| are) (?:diagnosed|definitely)\b

output_rules.description: Empty, truncated or repetitive output. Common failure mode in heavily quantized sub-billion-parameter models, so it must be caught rather than shown.

responses.self_harm:
It sounds like you may be going through something very difficult, and I'm sorry you're feeling this way. I can't help with this question, but please don't go through it alone — talk to someone you trust, or contact a health professional or emergency service right away.

[CONFIGURE: insert local emergency and mental-health contact numbers here before deployment]
responses.lethality:
I can't provide information about dangerous or harmful quantities of any medicine.

If you're worried that someone has taken too much of a medication, treat it as an emergency and get to a health facility or contact emergency services immediately.

[CONFIGURE: insert local emergency and poison-centre numbers here before deployment]
responses.dosage:
I can't give specific doses or dosing schedules — those depend on your weight, age, kidney and liver function, other medicines you take, and the condition being treated.

A pharmacist, nurse or doctor can give you the right dose. The leaflet inside the medicine package also carries the approved dosing information.

I can tell you what a medicine is generally used for, common side effects, and precautions to be aware of.
responses.paediatric:
I can't advise on medicines or doses for children. Children's doses depend on weight and age, and getting them wrong is dangerous.

Please speak to a pharmacist, nurse or doctor before giving any medicine to a child.
responses.pregnancy:
I can't advise on medication use during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Safety varies by medicine, by trimester, and by individual circumstances.

Please speak to a pharmacist, midwife, nurse or doctor, who can check your specific situation.
responses.stopping:
I can't advise on stopping, changing or replacing a prescribed medicine. Stopping some medicines suddenly is harmful.

Please speak to the health professional who prescribed it before making any change.
responses.misuse: I can only provide general information about the appropriate medical use of medicines. I can't help with this request.
responses.diagnosis:
I'm a medication-information assistant, so I can't tell you what condition you might have. A health professional can assess that properly.

I can explain what a particular medicine is used for, its common side effects, and precautions to be aware of.
responses.unavailable: I wasn't able to produce a reliable answer to that. Please rephrase your question, or ask a pharmacist or other health professional.
